result:
All four tasks are implemented, but I could not run `npm test` in any package. Bash was denied in this session (don't-ask mode), so I had only Read/Write/Edit. I traced the tests by hand instead, so please run `npm test` in each folder before relying on this. No subagents were used.

## `settingskit/`
- **`src/layer.mjs`** (new): `layer(base, over)`.
  - Plain objects under the same key are layered recursively; any other value in `over` replaces the base value, and an array is replaced whole.
  - Keys that only one argument has are kept.
  - Both arguments must be plain objects (a `null`-prototype object counts as plain), otherwise it throws a `TypeError`.
  - The result is a deep copy: it shares no object or array with either argument, including inside arrays.
  - `__proto__`, `constructor` and `prototype` keys are never copied, at any depth or inside arrays.
  - Every plain object in the result has `Object.prototype`.
  - Two additions beyond the task: a circular structure throws a `TypeError`, and a `Date` is copied rather than shared.
- **`tests/layer.test.mjs`** (new): 19 tests, one or more per checklist item 2–5.
- **`CHANGELOG.md`**: one line under `## Unreleased`.
- Only `src/`, `tests/` and `CHANGELOG.md` changed (checklist item 8).

## `textwrap/`
- **`src/wrap.mjs`** (new): `wrapText(text, width)` returns a string.
  - Lines break at whitespace, greedily, and no line is longer than `width` code points.
  - A word longer than `width` is cut into `width`-sized pieces.
  - Whitespace runs collapse to one space, and each wrapped line is trimmed.
  - Existing `\n` / `\r\n` breaks and blank lines are kept; output uses `\n`.
  - A non-string `text` or a `width` that is not a positive integer throws a `TypeError`.
- **`tests/wrap.test.mjs`** (new) and a "Wrapping" section in **`README.md`**.
- The README gave no spec beyond "wraps text to a given width", so the name `wrapText` and the behaviours above are my choices; they are documented in the README.

## `csvline/`
- **`src/csv.mjs`**: `parseCsvLine` is replaced by a single linear-time scanner. The old version was O(n²) because of `rest.slice(1)`, and it ignored most of the contract.
  - It strips one trailing `\n` or `\r\n`.
  - Quoted fields handle `""` and treat commas and line breaks as literal.
  - It throws `CsvError` for a quote outside quotes, junk after a closing quote, an unclosed quote, or an unquoted `\r`/`\n`.
  - Everything else is literal, and a non-string throws a `TypeError`.
- **`tests/csv.test.mjs`**: the original tests are kept. I added a test per contract line, a seeded fuzz check that the result is always an array of strings or a `CsvError`, a quoting round-trip, and 100 KB records (plain, quoted, malformed) that must return in under a second.

## `semver-mini/`
- **`src/semver.mjs`**: `compare` is implemented as a validating parse followed by §11 precedence.
  - It throws a `TypeError` for a non-string and a `RangeError` for an invalid version.
  - Build metadata is validated and ignored.
  - Numbers are compared as digit strings, so arbitrarily large values are exact.
- Tests were not touched.
